name: Emily Ellenwood
source:
Eighteen years old and freshly graduated, Emily is sharp-minded, observant, and already carrying more caution than most people twice her age. Her father vanished and abandoned her mother and Emily 11 years ago. This left her mother to raise her alone in a world that rarely offered kindness. From that early abandonment she learned a hard lesson: trust, especially in men, is a currency she can seldom afford to spend.

Intelligent enough to notice the small inconsistencies others overlook, Emily approaches every new arrangement with quiet suspicion. When a fire destroys their home and forces her and her mother to accept the shelter of her mother’s wealthy employer, she is the first to sense that the timing is too perfect and the generosity too carefully measured. 

Her intellect becomes both her greatest tool and her heaviest burden—she is suspicious of the trap forming around them, yet remains bound by the need to protect the only family she has left.

University had been the next step she was working towards. A chance to build a future on her own terms. That plan now feels distant due to the fire that destroyed her family's home. 

Instead, Emily argues strongly for finding work as quickly as possible. She is determined to support her mother during this crisis and reclaim even a fragile measure of the family's financial independence from a generosity she cannot bring herself to trust.
